connection.elsewhere: Once you get a hang of Ember, we recommend you give your Bots a separate place to work off of your computer. A container can be a good option for providing a seperate work environment. Another physical computer is also a good choice. These computers can keep working even if your close your laptop lid or close your computer entirely -  as long as their computer (and Kiln) stays on.
connection.existingBody: Enter that Kiln’s address and connection password. You can also do this later in Settings → Instances.
connection.heading: Choose where the work happens
connection.lead: Ember includes a Kiln on this computer, so you can start here. This enables the Bots to edit files and run commands. This Kiln stops when you quit Ember; the conversations are saved to your hard drive.
connection.okBody: Kiln is running on this computer and Ember has its token.
connection.otherBody: Install Ember there to get its own included Kiln. That Kiln starts and stops with that copy of Ember. Go into your settings and find the token. Use this password to connect to it from your main computer.
connection.prompt: Help me connect Ember on my personal computer to a standalone Kiln on [other computer] using Tailscale. Check how Kiln is installed and whether Tailscale is available on both computers. Configure the connection, keep Kiln's password out of source files, and verify that Ember can connect. Finish by telling me which address to enter in Ember and where to find the connection password.

connection.tailscaleBody: Use Tailscale to reach a separate Kiln on another computer.
connection.tailscaleNote: Tailscale connects the computers; Kiln’s connection password determines who can direct its bots.
connection.tailscaleStep1: Install Tailscale on both computers and connect them to the same Tailscale network.
connection.tailscaleStep2: Start Kiln with Tinder on the computer doing the work. For a container, make its Kiln port reachable from that computer’s Tailscale connection.
connection.tailscaleStep3: Find that computer’s Tailscale address in the Tailscale app, or run {code} there.
connection.tailscaleStep4: Add the Kiln below using an address such as {code} and the password printed by {code}. Use the port you chose for Kiln.
connection.tinderBody: Tinder is our launcher for Kiln without the Ember application. Download the matching Tinder executable from Ember’s releases and keep it in a permanent folder on the computer that will do the work.
connection.tinderFinish: Tinder prints the command to enable and start that service. Follow it, then add the address and password below.

first-agent.heading: Where does your work live?
first-agent.lead: Choose your workspace — the folder where you already keep your projects or work. You can pick a project inside it for each new chat. You can always acess folders elsewhere if you wish, as well.
first-agent.noHost: Connect a Kiln in the setup steps to choose a workspace.
first-agent.projectLead: Start in a project, or work directly in your workspace.
privacy.caveat: Your chosen AI provider receives the messages you send to it and the context your bots use, under that provider’s privacy policy. Ember also makes network requests for updates and model catalogues. Other than that, we track nothing.
privacy.heading: Free, open source, and private.
privacy.plain: Ember doesn’t send us analytics, crash reports, or bug reports. That means we won’t know when something breaks unless you tell us.
providers.afterwards: You can change all of this later in Settings → Providers (it saves as you go).
providers.emptyLead: Sign in or save an API key below. Once a provider is connected, choose your default model here.
providers.lead: Your bots need an AI service, such as OpenAI or Anthropic. Use a sign-in option below, or paste an API key — an access code you get from that service. If you use Ollama or LM Studio to run AI on your own computer, start it first and Ember will show it here.
providers.modelLead: Choose the model Ember will use for new bots on this instance. This does not change Kiln’s own default or existing conversations.
providers.modelNotReady: Choose an available model, then select Continue. If a model is missing, refresh models or connect another provider below.
providers.needsHost: Ember needs a connected Kiln before it can list providers or models. Retry this computer or connect another host.
providers.pasteKeyOr: Or paste an API key instead
providers.settingsMissing: Add an ember-harness endpoint first. Credentials live on each ember-harness host, not in this window.
providers.tipBody: No provider account yet? You can sign in or sign up on OpenCode’s website, which may offer free models. Availability and pricing can change; not every model is free. Copy an API key from OpenCode, paste it into OpenCode Zen below and select Save, then choose a model.

token.heading: Your token
token.hint: Other machines and browsers use this to connect to this one. Anyone who has it can use this computer's bots, so treat it like a password.
token.label: Token
token.lead: A token is a special password for computers to talk to each other. Kiln only answers clients that present its token.
token.localReady: Kiln is running here, and Ember already has its token — you only need to read it when you want to connect from another machine.
token.missing: There's no token to show: this build doesn't know about a harness on this computer.
token.noRotate: Ember didn't start this harness, so it can't give it a new token. Restart the harness yourself and it keeps the token it already has.
token.rotateWarning: Every other machine and browser pointed at this host will stop connecting until you copy the new token across. The bots themselves are untouched.

welcome.direct:
Ember is where you direct bots to do work, and observe the work they do. It connects to a piece of software behind the scenes called a Kiln. It's all set up for you here - but if you want to add another Kiln on another computer, you can set that up in minutes.

Kiln uses a harness called Pi behind the scenes, specifically the Pi-durable version, which is noted among experts for efficiency and reliablity across all models and providers.
welcome.heading: Where the work happens
welcome.hostContainerNote: A separate space on a computer
welcome.intro: Ember is an easy bot workspace where you can send out requests, review results and set scheduled messages. You see see each bot sesssion embodied in a cute little blob.  This, alongside other features, helps you use your agents more easily.
welcome.several: One Ember can connect to several Kilns that are running on various computers you've set up. Agents can even talk to each other across machines.
